claims.statement: Open-Inspect splits testing by ecosystem: all TypeScript packages use Vitest and all Python packages use pytest with pytest-asyncio (asyncio_mode = "auto"), wired into workspace scripts so `npm test` fans out across packages and Python suites run via `pytest tests/ -v`.

Test-file layout per package: control-plane unit tests are co-located as src/**/*.test.ts and run in the Node environment, control-plane integration tests live in test/integration/**/*.test.ts and run in workerd via @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers with real D1; web, slack-bot and linear-bot use co-located src tests; github-bot keeps tests in test/; modal-infra and sandbox-runtime use tests/test_*.py, with sandbox-runtime additionally shipping tests/*.test.mjs run by node --test.

The root vitest.workspace.ts defines the monorepo Vitest workspace as packages/*/vitest.config.ts, so every package's Vitest config participates in root-level runs; Node 22 is the minimum supported engine.

Control-plane unit tests (vitest.config.ts) run in the plain Node environment, include only src/**/*.test.ts, and collect v8 coverage over src/*.ts excluding test files, d.ts files, and the src/index.ts Worker entrypoint.

The control-plane integration config uses the cloudflareTest() Vite plugin from @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers against the test-only wrangler.jsonc Worker (SESSION Durable Object, D1 DB, REPOS_CACHE KV, MEDIA_BUCKET R2) with compatibilityDate 2024-09-23 and nodejs_compat to match the Terraform-managed production runtime.

Integration tests apply the real production D1 schema: the setup file test/integration/apply-migrations.ts runs applyD1Migrations(env.DB, env.TEST_MIGRATIONS), where the migration list is read from terraform/d1/migrations via readD1Migrations and injected as the TEST_MIGRATIONS binding.

Integration D1 isolation has two levels: @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers isolates D1 storage per test file so files run in parallel without interference, but within a file all tests share one D1 instance and must call cleanD1Tables() (a single env.DB.exec deleting every application table and resetting skills_catalog_state) in beforeEach/afterEach to avoid cross-test pollution.

The integration pool mocks all outbound networking through Miniflare's outboundService: *.modal.run requests return 404 (Modal is unavailable), OpenAI and xAI device-auth endpoints return canned credentials so device-code flows complete, and any unexpected outbound URL throws, so tests cannot silently leak network calls.

Integration test bindings are static test values mirroring production secrets: per-service SERVICE_AUTH_SECRET_* values equal the unit-test TEST_SERVICE_SECRETS, BROWSER_AUTH_SECRET is a long test secret, UNSAFE_ALLOW_ALL_USERS bypasses sign-in allowlists, and TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY/REPO_SECRETS_ENCRYPTION_KEY/PROVIDER_ACCOUNTS_ENCRYPTION_KEY are freshly generated 32-byte base64 AES keys because the SCM capture route encrypts inline and a placeholder would fail at runtime.

The integration config's onUnhandledError suppresses Better Auth APIError rejections (redirects and 401 INVALID_TOKEN) whose stacks originate inside better-auth/dist/api/routes/, since the library throws-and-catches them as HTTP responses and the Workers pool would otherwise report the intermediate rejection as unhandled.

Integration tests reach the worker through typed helpers: env.d.ts merges the production ControlPlaneEnv with the test-only TEST_MIGRATIONS binding so tests can pass env straight into production entrypoints; session-do-access.ts is the one seam that types SESSION stubs as SessionDO (runInSessionDO), reads the private runtime accessor to expose the component graph (componentsOf), and invokes the real user-env resolver (getUserEnvVars) — hand-synced, so renaming the DO's private accessor surfaces only as runtime TypeErrors.

The primary integration helper module (test/integration/helpers.ts) provides: initSession/initNamedSession/initNamedSessionDO (production-shaped D1 index row plus POST /internal/init to the SESSION DO stub), serviceFetch (per-request sig1 signing plus, for the web service, a real Better Auth user/session row and HMAC-signed __Secure-openinspect.session_token cookie), queryDO and waitForSandboxStatus (SQL polling of DO SqlStorage), seedEvents/seedMessage (direct DO SQLite inserts with correct timeline_sequence), seedSandboxAuth/seedSandboxAuthHash (waits for the always-failing test spawn to reach 'failed' so its status write cannot clobber the seeded row, then seeds auth_token(_hash), modal_sandbox_id and 'ready' status), and WebSocket helpers collectMessages/openClientWs/openSandboxWs driving the full SELF.fetch routing path.

Domain-specific integration seed helpers exist per area: run-helpers.ts does raw automation_runs/automation_invocations row seeding (the store no longer exposes single-run inserts), identity-seed-helpers.ts seeds canonical identity-registry rows at a fixed timestamp so epoch conversions are assertable, image-build-helpers.ts seeds environments and image_builds rows for the image-build suites, and google-id-token.ts mints real RS256-signed Google ID tokens for the sign-in claim tests.

The integration suite asserts execution semantics alongside routes: worker-fetch.test.ts covers routing basics and correlation headers via SELF.fetch, durable-object-eviction.test.ts forces DO eviction with state.abort() and reconstructs sockets from persisted wsid tags to prove WebSocket state survives eviction, and the scheduler/automation/image-build suites drive cron queue and runDurableObjectAlarm paths.

Unit router tests authenticate with signedServiceRequest from src/router.test-support.ts: sig1 binds method, URL and body, so every request is signed individually with test-service-secret-<service> via buildServiceAuthHeaders; the same TEST_SERVICE_SECRETS values are injected by the integration pool so unit and integration suites exercise identical credential material. Router suites also share one contract-faithful TEST_BACKGROUND_TASK_CONTEXT double.

createTestBackgroundTasks (src/background-tasks.test-support.ts) is a behaviorally identical double for the BackgroundTasks platform port: submit invokes the task factory synchronously, absorbs synchronous throws and async rejections into a failures list while recording submissions in order, and settle() drains all recorded tasks; background-tasks.test-support.test.ts pins the double to that production contract.

Control-plane typecheck runs three tsc programs — the production tsconfig, tsconfig.test.json, and the test/integration tsconfig — the last compiling integration files against workers types plus @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers/types without Node globals, mirroring their workerd execution context.

The shared package enforces module boundaries with a Vitest suite (src/module-boundaries.test.ts) that parses every production module via the TypeScript compiler API and asserts implementation modules never import the package-root or shared-types barrels, that there are no runtime dependency cycles, and that there are no compile-time dependency cycles; the dependency collector itself is unit-tested so import-type expressions stay compile-time-only.

ESLint-enforced boundaries are pinned in-repo by tests: web's client-auth-boundary-eslint.test.ts runs ESLint in-process to assert no-restricted-imports/no-restricted-globals boundaries (no direct NextAuth imports on the client, no raw browser fetch outside app-owned seams), and scripts/lint-complexity-message.test.mjs pins the complexity diagnostic parser run as npm run test:lint-complexity.

npm run lint:complexity (scripts/lint-complexity.mjs) runs ESLint's classic cyclomatic-complexity rule with max 0 across packages/**/*.{ts,tsx}, reporting production/test complexity distributions (>10/15/20/30/50) and production hotspots above 20; test files are excluded from the hotspot table, findings are report-only and never affect the exit code, and --json emits a machine-readable report.

Python config: both modal-infra and sandbox-runtime set asyncio_mode = "auto", extend the root ruff.toml (target py312, 100-column line length, rule set spanning pyflakes/isort/bugbear/comprehensions/pyupgrade/type-checking), and per AGENTS.md lint with `ruff check --fix && ruff format`; modal-infra's mypy runs strict but CI executes it with continue-on-error.

sandbox-runtime's conftest.py defines an autouse isolate_runtime_file_paths fixture that monkeypatches the runtime's fixed file paths (REPO_MANIFEST_FILE_PATH, BOOT_WARNINGS_FILE_PATH, TUNNEL_ENV_FILE_PATH) to per-test tmp_path locations, because the suite routinely runs inside a live Open-Inspect sandbox (agents dogfooding the repo) where the real files belong to the running session and a test driving a real SandboxSupervisor would otherwise overwrite live session state.

sandbox-runtime tests use shared utilities in conftest.py and runtime_helpers.py: wire_opencode_transport rebuilds a bridge's OpenCode client around a fake HTTP transport test seam, oc_message_id builds deterministic OpenCode ascending message IDs so boundary tests can place IDs relative to a prompt's user message, MockResponse scripts HTTP responses, and make_supervisor/make_repository_boot construct real runtime objects with synthetic env and a tmp_path workspace.

modal-infra tests never touch real Modal or the network: test_sandbox_launch.py parametrizes base/repository/snapshot image sources and monkeypatches modal.Sandbox.create, _resolve_and_setup_tunnels, and password generation to assert the launch behavior matrix.

TypeScript CI (ci.yml) runs ESLint, test:lint-complexity, Prettier check, Knip, typecheck (which builds @open-inspect/shared first because dependent packages import it at build time), web build, shared+control-plane unit tests, control-plane integration tests sharded 1/2 and 2/2, web tests, and bot tests; Python CI (ci-python.yml) runs Ruff lint and format checks, pytest for modal-infra and sandbox-runtime, node --test for runtime JS tests, and MyPy with continue-on-error.

A containerized integration path exists: packages/control-plane/Dockerfile.test copies shared + control-plane + terraform/d1/migrations into a node:22-slim image with libc++1 (workerd prerequisite), builds @open-inspect/shared, and runs npm run test:integration -w @open-inspect/control-plane as its CMD.

Completion conventions encoded across the repo: build @open-inspect/shared first or typecheck and integration tests fail (dependents import it at build time), run npm run typecheck and lint:complexity before considering a change complete, use seconds for Python durations and milliseconds for TypeScript with the unit encoded in the name, and treat source code and tests as authoritative over briefs.
